answer: A strong defence is to tie each identity to a costly, non-transferable work history: an agent must complete verified, useful tasks over time before it gains full earning rights, and misbehaviour burns its accumulated reputation. A single attacker can fake one profile cheaply, but cloning that history across hundreds of identities is like trying to build a wharf on tundra over crumbling shale — each new identity needs its own slow, expensive foundation, so Sybil farming stops paying.
